Go with what the blade is already at. Usually the factory gets it right. Hold the knife flat to the stone, then raise the back end up until the blade rests flush and there us no shadow between it and the stone, then raise up just a teeny bit more and that's the angle you should sharpen at.

My advice if you want the most out of the blade is to get a leather strop and use it often, I tend to strop my knives almost daily whether I use them or not, stropping just polishes the edge and gets rid of any micro burrs and serrations.

Also for a guided beginner sharpener I can't recommend this enough, https://www.worksharptools.com/guided-field-sharpener.html

I've always been good at sharpening with almost anything, at home I use a whetstone and a coffee cup, but I've used rocks and bricks files etc.. and Even I carry a Worksharp in the bush all the time. It has guides but you are not forced to use them you can freely sharpen how you want but the guides would be great for learning. It also has a lifetime warranty and all that good stuff.
